facts.value: Resolves a fighter joint and submits kind-dependent requests through efAsync_Spawn using fp->x60C as queue head. Generic and second-switch paths copy arg5 and add three sequential centered random samples scaled by arg6. Kind-7 cases and 0x49D instead use unchanged offsets; 0x49D uses arg6.x to compute an angle. Other special paths supply fighter/common scalar data. IDs 0x513..0x515 emit camera-quake kind 8 with IDs 2..4. efAsync_Spawn copies vector/scalar values before returning and retains the joint pointer, not pointers to caller-local parameters.
facts.rationale: Corrects universal randomization and distinguishes request storage, special angular input, and quake routing.

evidence.why: Active consumer establishes copying, joint retention, world-position conversion, and camera routing.

facts.value: Declared void(Fighter_GObj*, int, Fighter_Part, int, int, Vec3*, Vec3*, float). Following the fighter object, parameters provide graphics ID, part selector, ordinary-part remapping flag, fighter-effect marker flag, offset vector, kind-dependent spread/angular vector, and an unused final float. A direct animation-command call is verified; callback registration and register-locator assignments are not established.
facts.rationale: Canonical signature and all parameter uses outrank an inferred callback classification.

facts.value: Implements fighter animation-driven graphics requests, including particle/effect spawning from selected model joints with animation-supplied placement and effect-specific orientation or scale. Some kinds forward the joint, others convert its offset to world position, and IDs 0x513..0x515 request camera quakes. Persistent joint attachment is not universal.
facts.rationale: Retains the verified conceptual mapping while repairing the baseline's overbroad attachment description.

evidence.why: Animation graphics command supplies the request.
Active routing distinguishes attachment, position, and quake paths.

facts.value: Appends bytes 80 00 81 00 8E 01 91 B0 8E 01 81 00 8E 0A 80 00 7F through eight two-byte emitters and one byte emitter to fp->cpu.write_pos. Successful completion advances the cursor 17 bytes without resetting it or activating csP. Each byte writer checks the upper buffer bound; a valid initialized cursor and sufficient remaining space are required, and a later assertion can follow a partial append.
facts.rationale: Replaces obsolete member naming and records non-atomic writer preconditions.

facts.value: A void(Fighter*) CPU command construction helper. It forwards the Fighter pointer unchanged to emitters accessing struct CpuFighter through fp->cpu and appending to write_pos. No compiled offset or historical Fighter_x1A88_t identity is asserted.
facts.rationale: Uses canonical source type and member rather than historical aliases.

facts.value: Contains fighter animation-driven graphics dispatch: model joints and animation-supplied offsets feed joint-forwarding effects, world-position effects, or camera quakes, with kind-specific facing, scale, attribute, and floor-angle data. The TU also contains a fixed CPU virtual-controller script constructor; it does not establish a named gameplay maneuver.
facts.rationale: Repairs universal attachment wording and represents both independently verified TU responsibilities.

facts.value: The graphics dispatcher sets fighter-wide x2219_b0 only for nonzero arg4 and resolves special part selectors before graphics validation. Selector 0x8D normally cycles five entries, assuming a valid initial index because the read precedes wrap. State-change code consults the marker when KeepGfx is absent. Floor-angle paths use atan2f(-normal.x,normal.y) only for GA_Ground and otherwise zero. Unsupported second-switch IDs still consume three random samples after earlier flag/counter side effects, then report no effect. The CPU helper independently appends a fixed terminated stream without activating it.
facts.rationale: Avoids per-request ownership and side-effect-free unsupported-ID implications.

evidence.why: Angles, random draws, diagnostic, and command append.
